0.0.n: This is a person's name here, not the food 豆腐.

0.1.n: Attached to a name to show respect without specifying gender.

0.2.n: Marks Tofu-san as the person this sentence is about.

0.4.n: A personal pronoun commonly used by male speakers.

0.5.n: Links 僕 to 誕生日, making it the speaker's birthday.

0.6.n: With 僕の, this refers to the speaker's special day.

0.7.n: Marks the birthday as the time or occasion of the gift.

0.8.n: A borrowed word naming the item the speaker received.

0.9.n: Shows that ボールペン is the thing given.

0.10.n: Polite past form of くれる, used when someone gives something to the speaker or someone close to them.

1.0.n: Points back to the pen mentioned in the previous sentence and goes directly before a noun.

1.1.n: Here it refers to the same writing instrument Tofu-san gave the speaker.

1.2.n: Marks the pen as what the speaker is now talking about.

1.4.n: With の after it, this pronoun identifies whose treasure the pen is.

1.5.n: Links 僕 to 宝物 to express ownership.

1.6.n: Used for a cherished possession, not necessarily something expensive.

1.7.n: Politely ends the statement identifying the pen as the speaker's treasure.

2.0.n: Connects the speaker's wish to give a gift with the reason explained earlier.

2.2.n: This is the same person's name as in the first sentence.

2.3.n: Shows respect toward Tofu when attached to the name.

2.4.n: Links 豆腐さん to 誕生日, identifying whose birthday it is.

2.5.n: This time, the special day belongs to Tofu-san rather than the speaker.

2.6.n: Marks Tofu-san's birthday as the intended occasion for giving the gift.

2.7.n: Added after に to highlight this birthday, with a possible contrast to the speaker's birthday.

2.9.n: Describes the intended gift and needs な before the noun.

2.10.n: Connects 素敵 to プレゼント so it describes the gift.

2.11.n: A borrowed word for the item the speaker wants to give Tofu-san.

2.12.n: Marks プレゼント as the thing the speaker wants to give.

2.13.n: あげる becomes あげたい to express the speaker's wish to give to someone else; です adds politeness.

0.lit: As for Tofu-san, on my birthday, a ballpoint pen, gave me.
0.tip: くれる shows giving toward the speaker, so the recipient me can be left unstated.

1.lit: As for that ballpoint pen, my treasure it is.
1.tip: その points back to something already mentioned: the pen received as a gift.

2.lit: So, as for on Tofu-san's birthday, a wonderful gift I want to give.
2.tip: あげたい expresses wanting to give to someone else, contrasting with くれました, which described receiving from someone.
